sectionHeadings: 3.3 What an ad-hoc signature costs, stated plainly
record.summary: The route from this checkout to a running Butler on the developer's own Mac, which no spec claimed: a `make dev` hot-reload loop and a `make app` that produces an ad-hoc signed `Butler.app` and installs it. It needs no Developer ID, no notarization and no repository secret, because nothing it produces is published: the artifact carries no authority in its signature and says so. Spec 017 is untouched and still governs anything a stranger downloads. The costs an ad-hoc signature imposes, chiefly that macOS re-asks for Screen Recording after every rebuild, are written down rather than papered over.
record.title: Local development builds: run and install Butler on your own machine without a signing identity
